messages.subject: Problems using srvyr package to calculcate standard error using replicate weights
parts:
Hi All,

 

Anyone have experience calculating standard error for PUMS-based estimates using replicate weights?


I’m using the srvyr package to calculate standard errors of estimates using PUMS data and PUMS replicate weights. I’m finding that the SEs I get using the srvyr package are consistently about half the size of the SEs I get with manual calculations. My manual SE calculations match the PUMS Estimates for User Verification.


I'd like to use the srvyr package, or at the very least understand what is going wrong here.

See my reproducible example here:
http://ldaly.github.io/Learning/reproducible-question-script.html

parts:
Hi Laura, 

I don’t know enough about srvyr to answer your question directly.  Searching around suggests that srvyr::survey_total() is supposed to be using survey::svytotal() under the hood, but sometimes things aren’t passed back and forth correctly (cf https://github.com/gergness/srvyr/issues/29).  Do survey::svyby() and survey::svytotal() give you the correct or erroneous results?  

Dan

parts:
Hi All,

Dan, thanks for getting back to me. Your response prompted me to take a deeper dive into the survey package, which ultimately led me to the answer. 

Both survey:svytotal() and srvyr::survey_total() were giving me similar SE results, until I specified the scale and rscale arguments. Once I did that, functions from both packages are giving me good-looking results.

For anyone who is interested, this looks like:

Using the srvyr package
repweights = rep(paste0("PWGTP",1:80))

pumsd <- ppl_0_14 %>%
  as_survey_rep(
    variables = agegrp,
    weights = PWGTP,
    repweights = repweights,
    combined_weights = TRUE,
    mse =TRUE,
    type="other",
    scale=4/80,
    rscale=rep(1,80)
  )


# calculate pop and SE
  pumsd %>%
  group_by(agegrp) %>%
  summarise(
    count = survey_total())



Using the survey package

svydesigntst <-
survey::svrepdesign(data=ppl_0_14,
                    weights= ppl_0_14[,9],
                    repweights=ppl_0_14[,17:96],
                   combined.weights=TRUE,
                   type="other",
                   scale=4/80,
                   rscales=rep(1,80))


survey::svytotal(~agegrp, svydesigntst)
